raw_response:
I do what I always do. My two mu, one piece wheat in winter, one piece maize in summer, like my father did, like I have done for fifty-five years. My boy brings me seed from the village shop in October — the shopkeeper tells me which one people are buying this year, I take that one. Same for maize seed in June. The big bags, the hybrid ones, everyone plants them now. The old seed from my grandfather's time, nobody keeps that.

Fertilizer I buy at the shop too. For wheat on my two mu I put down three bags of the compound — the 15-15-15 one — before I plough. That is my base. Then when wheat is greening up in spring I spread one bag of urea, maybe a little more if the leaves look yellow. My neighbor Old Wang does the same. If I put less, I am afraid the wheat will be thin. Losing harvest is worse than spending a few extra yuan on fertilizer.

For maize after wheat, I do not plough again, I just rotary till the stubble. I put two bags compound at sowing, then one bag of urea at knee-high when I hoe the weeds. Maize eats less than wheat I find, but still needs feeding.

Water I have from the well, so I turn the pump on. Wheat needs water — once before winter so the roots hold, once at greening, once when it is making the head, once when the grain is filling. Four times if the sky does not rain. Maize in summer usually gets rain, but if July is dry I irrigate once or twice.

Pesticide — I spray twice on wheat, once for aphids in spring, once when heading. Maize I spray once for the borer worm, sometimes twice if I see them. The shop sells me the bottle, tells me how much to mix in the sprayer.

Ploughing — I hire the tractor man from the village, he does rotary tilling for thirty yuan a mu. Only before wheat I ask him to plough deeper. After wheat for maize, no ploughing, just rotary, faster that way and maize still grows fine.

Good year I get nine hundred jin of wheat on my two mu, that is four hundred fifty jin per mu. Maize a bit more, five hundred fifty jin per mu. Enough to sell some, keep some flour for us two old people.
